utterances.text: One moment before, can -- I'm sure it's not my eyesight. Can we have a better focusing on the document, please. Yes, that's perfect. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] My signature is at the entries of the 11th, the 13th, the 17th, the 15th, the 18th -- is it the 18th? Yes. The 19th, the 21st, and the 24th.

utterances.speaker: MR. THAYER
utterances.text: Okay. Thank you, sir. We are done with that document. Now, sir, I want to turn your attention to the document that you testified about involving a Mr. Gotovac. Do you remember the vehicle work log for the Volkswagen van?

utterances.speaker: MIRKO SAKOTIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. THAYER
utterances.text: Is it fair to say that from the day that you signed off on that document, you did not see it again until it was shown to you by the Nikolic Defence team?

utterances.speaker: MIRKO SAKOTIC
utterances.text: It may well be so that I didn't see it in the meantime. I don't remember viewing it much. As far as I can see, my signature is there only for the 14th, and I seem to be the one who sent him to the lines.

utterances.speaker: MR. THAYER
utterances.text: Now, I think you said in your statement that on that day you issued a lot of vehicle work orders?

utterances.speaker: MIRKO SAKOTIC
utterances.text: Yes, just like any other day.

utterances.speaker: MR. THAYER
utterances.text: Just like any other day during the war, sir; correct?

utterances.speaker: MIRKO SAKOTIC
utterances.text: Yes. It was a regular day.

utterances.speaker: MR. THAYER
utterances.text: And out of all the orders that you signed off on, out of all the routes that you signed off on and your time in the transportation section, you had no reason to see, let alone remember, this log after you issued it on the 14th of July; correct?

utterances.speaker: MIRKO SAKOTIC
utterances.text: I didn't see it. There were many orders, things kept developing and we were under a lot of burden.

utterances.speaker: MR. THAYER
utterances.text: Mr. President, if we may jump into private session very briefly, please.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: By all means. Let's go into private session for a short while, please. We are in private session.

utterances.speaker: MR. THAYER
utterances.text: Now, sir, I want to show you another document.

utterances.speaker: MR. THAYER
utterances.text: If we could have 65 ter 295 again, please. P00295. And if I've got the numbers right, we are at page 541 of the English and page 539 of the B/C/S.

utterances.speaker: MR. THAYER
utterances.text: And with Madam Usher's assistance, I'm going to hand you the original of this document, sir, because I think it will be much easier for you to read if you are looking at the original. Sir, we are looking at another vehicle work log. This one for a Rovokopac and that's a backhoe excavator; correct?

utterances.speaker: MIRKO SAKOTIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. THAYER
utterances.text: And we can see that there's information that has been typed in, and I think you'll agree with me if you're looking at the original that you can see that has been done with a typewriter or some sort of typewriting device as opposed to --

utterances.speaker: MIRKO SAKOTIC
utterances.text: It was typewritten, yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. THAYER
utterances.text: For those of us who are trying to follow along in e-court, there is a mistake in terms of the document that's being shown. We are looking for the ERN that ends in 5083, please. That's 539 in B/C/S.

utterances.speaker: MR. THAYER
utterances.text: Now, sir, you'll agree with me that the information that's typed in with respect to the piece of equipment and the operators is separate from the handwriting that you see in the blue ink on the bottom half of the document; correct? The top is typewritten, the bottom is handwritten in ink?

utterances.speaker: MR. THAYER
utterances.text: It might help the visibility if we take the document out of the plastic, please, on the ELMO. Thank you, Madam Usher.

utterances.speaker: MR. THAYER
utterances.text: You'll agree with me that is Mr. Pantic's signature in the lower right-hand corner under number 2 or next to number 2? Now -- forgive me, sir.

utterances.speaker: MIRKO SAKOTIC
utterances.text: No, that is my signature.

utterances.speaker: MR. THAYER
utterances.text: It wasn't a trick question. I tricked myself. Whose signature is that, sir?

utterances.speaker: MIRKO SAKOTIC
utterances.text: Mine.

utterances.speaker: MR. THAYER
utterances.text: Okay. And can you read the date of the single entry that is handwritten there in ink?

utterances.speaker: MIRKO SAKOTIC
utterances.text: The 14th of July, 1995.

utterances.speaker: MR. THAYER
utterances.text: If we could turn the document over, please. That will be the next page in B/C/S, please, as well as the English translation.

utterances.speaker: MR. THAYER
utterances.text: Can you read that top line, sir?

utterances.speaker: MIRKO SAKOTIC
utterances.text: Base, Orahovac and back.

utterances.speaker: MR. THAYER
utterances.text: That's for trench digging. And if we go down to the bottom of the page, sir?

utterances.speaker: MIRKO SAKOTIC
utterances.text: Yes, digging trenches.

utterances.speaker: MR. THAYER
utterances.text: And if we go down to the bottom of the page, it says 6 hours of use.

utterances.speaker: MIRKO SAKOTIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. THAYER
utterances.text: Now, having had a chance to look at this document, you recalled a lot about the log that involved Mr. Gotovac and that trip. Can you tell the Trial Chamber what this backhoe/excavator was being used for in Orahovac for those six hours that are indicated?

utterances.speaker: MIRKO SAKOTIC
utterances.text: As you can see from the work order, it was the traffic section and the rear brigade that sent the work order. The rest of the entries was done outside the traffic section. Even the fuel was not taken from the gas station.

utterances.speaker: MR. THAYER
utterances.text: Now, if you flip the document over, sir, to the first page or the front page, there's an operator by the name of Cvijetin Ristanovic. Do you know that person, sir?

utterances.speaker: MIRKO SAKOTIC
utterances.text: It sounds familiar. The name strikes me as familiar, but I'm sure I don't know what he looks like.

utterances.speaker: MR. THAYER
utterances.text: Well, the Trial Chamber has heard evidence from Mr. Ristanovic as well as survivors of a mass execution in the Orahovac area. And Mr. Ristanovic testified that he used that backhoe excavator to dig a mass grave while the executions were still going on in front of him. Do you know anything about that, sir?

utterances.speaker: MIRKO SAKOTIC
utterances.text: No, not at all.

utterances.speaker: MR. THAYER
utterances.text: Okay. We are done with that document, thank you. Now, I just want to show you a couple of more documents. And ask you about, again, these ten days or so following the fall of Srebrenica on 11 July. Do you recall following the fall of Srebrenica that there were urgent requests coming to the brigade from the battalions for extra ammunition, fuel, shells, artillery rounds?

utterances.speaker: MIRKO SAKOTIC
utterances.text: It was a long time ago, I really don't remember. I didn't issue shells or ammunition. I only had to do with vehicles. I really can't remember what the activities undertaken were. It was quite sometime ago.

utterances.speaker: MR. THAYER
utterances.text: Okay. Well, you spent your time during this period of time and prior to the fall of Srebrenica in the command, in the logistics unit. Is there anything about that ten days to two weeks after the fall of Srebrenica that sticks out in your mind in terms of what was going on in the Zvornik Brigade's area of responsibility?

utterances.speaker: MIRKO SAKOTIC
utterances.text: I remember the things known by everybody. I remember that people were talking about the child the next day or the day after that. Then I also heard that Pilica was being mentioned, Orahovac, Petkovci and Rocevic. That was the rumours. I didn't -- I wasn't present at any of these locations, therefore, I can't tell you anything more than that.

utterances.speaker: MR. THAYER
utterances.text: Well, let's use, say, the 14th of July as a starting point. You talked about that date. Can you tell the Trial Chamber approximately how soon after that date you started hearing rumours, for example, about the child that you just referred to? How soon did you start hearing rumours about the child?

utterances.speaker: MIRKO SAKOTIC
utterances.text: Probably the next day or in the next couple of days. I can't remember exactly. There was so much going on that I truly can't say.

utterances.speaker: MR. THAYER
utterances.text: And you just mentioned several locations, Pilica, Orahovac, Petkovci, and Rocevic, what were the rumours that you were hearing, sir?

utterances.speaker: MIRKO SAKOTIC
utterances.text: Well, the rumour had it that people were being killed there, something like that. I really don't know. I wasn't there. There were stories going around and that's it.

utterances.speaker: MR. THAYER
utterances.text: And again, using the 14th of July as a benchmark date, how soon after that date did you start hearing these rumours about Pilica and Rocevic and Petkovci and Orahovac?

utterances.speaker: MIRKO SAKOTIC
utterances.text: I really can't recall.

utterances.speaker: MR. THAYER
utterances.text: Well, was it within a matter of days?

utterances.speaker: MIRKO SAKOTIC
utterances.text: It was a really long time ago. Probably even today you can still hear stories going around.

utterances.speaker: MR. THAYER
utterances.text: Well, can you tell the Trial Chamber what your best recollection is then, sir, of when you started hearing these rumours about executions at these locations that you just mentioned?

utterances.speaker: MIRKO SAKOTIC
utterances.text: I'm telling you that I cannot remember. Even if I tried my best, I still wouldn't be able to remember.

utterances.speaker: MR. THAYER
utterances.text: Not even whether it was a month, six months, or a year?

utterances.speaker: MIRKO SAKOTIC
utterances.text: Not a year later but shorter than that. I don't know how much shorter though.

utterances.speaker: MR. THAYER
utterances.text: May we have 65 ter 295 if it's still up. And we'll be looking at page 583 of the English and page 581 of the B/C/S.

utterances.speaker: MR. THAYER
utterances.text: You see the document in front of you, sir, and can you read it? Is it legible to you?

utterances.speaker: MIRKO SAKOTIC
utterances.text: Yes, I can.

utterances.speaker: MR. THAYER
utterances.text: As you can see, it's a vehicle work log for a TAM 130. It's driven by or operated by Milenko Tomic. Do you know Milenko Tomic, sir?

utterances.speaker: MIRKO SAKOTIC
utterances.text: Yes. He was a driver in the logistics brigade.

utterances.speaker: MR. THAYER
utterances.text: And if we look to the left of the document, again under the conditions, do you see Mr. Pantic's signature on the 17th?

utterances.speaker: MIRKO SAKOTIC
utterances.text: Yes, yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. THAYER
utterances.text: And if we go to the next page in e-court, please. If we look at that first line, you see the date of 17 July 1995, sir?

utterances.speaker: MIRKO SAKOTIC
utterances.text: Yes, I do.

utterances.speaker: MR. THAYER
utterances.text: And the route is Zvornik-Pilica-Kula-Pilica-Zvornik, do you see that, sir?

utterances.speaker: MIRKO SAKOTIC
utterances.text: Yes, I do.

utterances.speaker: MR. THAYER
utterances.text: If we go all the way to column 20, do you see Mr. Pantic's signature again, sir?

utterances.speaker: MIRKO SAKOTIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. THAYER
utterances.text: Next to his name is written "Slavko," do you see that, sir?

utterances.speaker: MIRKO SAKOTIC
utterances.text: Yes, I do. It probably is Slavko.

utterances.speaker: MR. THAYER
utterances.text: Do you know who that refers to?

utterances.speaker: MIRKO SAKOTIC
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. THAYER
utterances.text: And right below Mr. Pantic's signature, we have your signature for three entries in a row, is that correct, in column 20?

utterances.speaker: MIRKO SAKOTIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. THAYER
utterances.text: And then following that we've got Mr. Pantic's signature for another three lines?

utterances.speaker: MIRKO SAKOTIC
utterances.text: That's correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. THAYER
utterances.text: And this is for a period of approximately ten days from the 17th through the 27th, and this indicates, does it not, that you and Mr. Pantic are in the command together, working interchangeably; correct?

utterances.speaker: MIRKO SAKOTIC
utterances.text: Yes. We did our job in that time period, that's correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. THAYER
utterances.text: Now, Mr. Tomic testified before this Trial Chamber that Mr. Pantic personally ordered him to go to Pilica where he used this TAM 130 to transport corpses from the Pilica Dom to the Branjevo farm. And the Trial Chamber has also heard testimony from another soldier who had to load those corpses on to that truck and then unload them at the Branjevo farm. You referred a few moments ago to hearing rumours about executions at Pilica.

utterances.speaker: MIRKO SAKOTIC
utterances.text: Yes, I heard.

utterances.speaker: MR. THAYER
utterances.text: Does this help you determine when you knew that there were executions going on at Pilica, sir? Does this document help you in any way?

utterances.speaker: MIRKO SAKOTIC
utterances.text: No, I don't think so. Not at all.

utterances.speaker: MR. THAYER
utterances.text: Do you know anything, sir, about a reburial operation in the fall of 1995, to dig up corpses and redistribute them among smaller scattered mass graves? Do you know anything about that operation or the logistical needs that it required from the brigade?

utterances.speaker: MIRKO SAKOTIC
utterances.text: Absolutely nothing.

utterances.speaker: MR. THAYER
utterances.text: If I may have a moment, Mr. President.

utterances.speaker: MR. THAYER
utterances.text: Thank you, sir. I have no further questions.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Ms. Nikolic, is there redirect?

utterances.speaker: MS. NIKOLIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Just two or three questions, Your Honour. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MS. NIKOLIC
utterances.text: Mr. Sakotic, as you were answering my questions and the questions put to you by my colleague about the issuing and receiving orders, when you received an order from the duty operations officer, was that the person who only relayed the order to you from the assistant commander for logistics?

utterances.speaker: MIRKO SAKOTIC
utterances.text: Well, he probably consulted somebody as he issued the orders, but more or less based on logic --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. Thayer.

utterances.speaker: MR. THAYER
utterances.text: Just to make sure the record is accurate. I don't think there was any testimony, nor did I refer to a duty operations officer, but you know, I stand to be corrected if there is a citation somewhere. Maybe it's a translation issue.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Shall we check that or --

utterances.speaker: MS. NIKOLIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I may have, Your Honours -- I do believe my learned colleague is right, but let me move on to another topic, and I do apologise.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Go ahead, then.

utterances.speaker: MS. NIKOLIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MS. NIKOLIC
utterances.text: When you spoke about this word, loko, local drive, you said they were about 2 or 3 kilometres long. My question to you is how far is Orahovac from Zvornik?

utterances.speaker: MIRKO SAKOTIC
utterances.text: 7 to 9 kilometres, closer to 9, I think. I can't really remember for some reason, but it's a separate trip. A new trip. It's not considered as a local trip.

utterances.speaker: MS. NIKOLIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Could we please move into private session for my next question, Your Honours, to avoid --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Yes, go into private session, please. We are in private session, Ms. Nikolic.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Ms. Nikolic, I see you conferring with Mr. Bourgon. Have you finished with your redirect or not?

utterances.speaker: MS. NIKOLIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes, I have.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: All right. So unless any of my colleagues wish to put questions. Mr. Sakotic, we've come to the end of your testimony. Our staff will assist you and arrange for your return back home. On behalf of the Trial Chamber, I wish to thank you for having come over and given testimony. And on behalf of everyone I wish you a safe journey back home.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you very much, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Ms. Nikolic, documents?

utterances.speaker: MS. NIKOLIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honours, I think that the list has been handed in.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: One is the witness statement that, basically, we already know there's no objection to.

utterances.speaker: MS. NIKOLIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: And the other one is the vehicle log with markings done by the witness. Any objection?

utterances.speaker: MR. THAYER
utterances.text: No objection, Mr. President.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: No objection from the other Defence teams either. So these two documents.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Ms. Nikolic, I think we can work out like that. I'm being reminded by our staff that the arrangement was that you would provide two versions of the statement of this witness. One of which would have the name of a particular witness redacted. What you have used today is the unredacted copy or version, which means that we need to preserve it under seal; correct?

utterances.speaker: MS. NIKOLIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] That's correct, sir. Thank you very much for this intervention, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: [Previous translation continues] ... we are keeping it under seal. Both documents are therefore admitted. The first one of which will be under seal. Mr. Thayer?

utterances.speaker: MR. THAYER
utterances.text: Mr. President, we would tender just one document, that was 65 ter 3742, the page from the brigade telephone book.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Any objection?

utterances.speaker: MS. NIKOLIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] No, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Thank you. So that document is also admitted. And we can proceed to our next witness.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: We need to interview this witness first before we decide.

utterances.speaker: MR. BOURGON
utterances.text: Mr. President, if with your or with the Trial Chamber's permission, I would like to address the Trial Chamber before the witness comes in.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: All right. Okay. Let's go into closed session, I suppose.

utterances.speaker: MR. BOURGON
utterances.text: Indeed, Mr. President, please.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Let's go into closed session, please. There are no people in the gallery. Please don't admit anyone in the gallery for the time being, that avoids us having to put down curtains and whatever.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Now, we can leave. 25 minutes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. Bourgon.

utterances.speaker: MR. BOURGON
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. President.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: We are in open session. If you want to go in closed session, we'll go in closed session.

utterances.speaker: MR. BOURGON
utterances.text: I don't think it is required to go into private session, however, I do would like to make some submissions regarding the request for protective measures with the leave of the Trial Chamber.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Yeah, but what I meant was whether you prefer to make these submissions in open session or in closed session.

utterances.speaker: MR. BOURGON
utterances.text: I believe to be on the safe side it should be in private session, Mr. President.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Fine. Then let's go into private or closed session.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: So we are back in open session. Thank you for your submissions as you would have imagined, during the break we did have a thorough discussion ourselves on this, and subject to what we were anticipating to hear from you as further submissions, which we've just heard now, we reserved our judgement until later. We are actually in this situation where the majority are not in favour of granting the protective measures sought by this witness or on behalf of this witness. However, since this is not a unanimous decision, we thought of coming back to you with the same suggestion that we made in the past on a few occasions when we denied protective measures, namely, that we appeal to you to reach some kind of an agreement. For example, that you will not refer to him by his name, to avoid putting questions indicating where he lives, where he works, and such like arrangements. Even on one occasion, I think we had an arrangement whereby it was agreed that the cameraman will not focus on his face. However, we are not in a position to grant the protective measures that you requested, Ms. Nikolic and Mr. Bourgon. I believe that there are no sufficient grounds for granting them and it would constitute an undesirable precedent if we did. Do you wish to approach each other and have a word?

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: I'll certainly agree not to mention his name and have the audio folks agree that they do not show his face. I don't have a problem with that.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Mr. Bourgon.

utterances.speaker: MR. BOURGON
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. President. I -- with the Court's permission, I would like to obtain a short recess so I can go and meet with the witness. That being said, Mr. President, we are in an unprecedented situation. When the Court has asked questions before to a witness on the protective measures, to my recollection, that was done before the witness took the oath. This witness has taken the oath, so I would like the permission of the Court to go and meet with the witness and discuss with him and come back before the Trial Chamber.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Okay. You discuss this and only this with him, obviously.

utterances.speaker: MR. BOURGON
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. President.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: We have five minutes break or as soon as you finish please, you'll let us know. We'll be outside.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: --- Break taken at 6.31 p.m.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. Bourgon.

utterances.speaker: MR. BOURGON
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. President.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: We are in open session.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Or we redact, we just redact. Okay. Do you want private session?

utterances.speaker: MR. BOURGON
utterances.text: I'll say it in private session simply to tell you, Mr. President --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: No problem. We go into private session.

utterances.speaker: MR. BOURGON
utterances.text: Just for this one bit.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: We are in open session. Now for the record, the witness has been withdrawn and Mr. Bourgon gave an explanation why. What is next. We have got 10 minutes. I don't suppose we have another witness here present today?

utterances.speaker: MR. BOURGON
utterances.text: Mr. President, we are ready to proceed with another witness as we will be during all of our Defence case as much as we can be. The witness is here, he can take his oath now, and we can proceed with his testimony in the morning. Mr. President, I take this opportunity if I can obtain a confirmation that the Trial Chamber will be issuing a written decision, is that my understanding or that's what I thought I understood from what you said earlier.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: We had no intention of issuing a written decision, no.

utterances.speaker: MR. BOURGON
utterances.text: Then it's my mistake, Mr. President. We will be asking for certification of the decision.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: If you insist on one, we will provide you with one.

utterances.speaker: MR. BOURGON
utterances.text: No, we don't insist at all. I thought that was my understanding and it's my --

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: The interpreters are not able to hear what the speakers are saying because of the background noise.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: All right. Okay so let's repeat because there was too much background noise.

utterances.speaker: MR. BOURGON
utterances.text: Sorry, Mr. President. I was under the impression that the Trial Chamber had said that it would issue a judgement later, but I obviously made a mistake so I apologise. I simply say that we will, of course, be applying for certification of the Trial Chamber's decision in order to get a criteria for the Appeals Chamber. Thank you, Mr. President.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Thank you. Yes, Mr. McCloskey.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: Well, if he is going to appeal this kind of thing and having put this explanation on the record, I have an alternative explanation of why this person isn't testifying as a possibility as well.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Yes. Let's --

utterances.speaker: MR. BOURGON
utterances.text: What does that have to do with it, Mr. President.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Stop, Mr. Bourgon. I think at this stage it's all over. So let's leave it at that and, I mean, his right to seek certification is not subject to -- you can reply to that when he files the appropriate motion.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. President. I wasn't going to be objecting to his right to seek certification. He offered the reasons why this person couldn't be here based on his discussion with him, so that is going to be part of the appellate record. I could put in the Prosecution's view of that, but given that it's late, I think I'll just sit down.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: All right.

utterances.speaker: MR. BOURGON
utterances.text: Mr. President, I'm sorry. I have to reply to this.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: No. We don't want to hear any more on this, Mr. Bourgon. If you want to file a motion for --

utterances.speaker: MR. BOURGON
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. President.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: -- you file it and then it will take its course. If you want a written decision, we will provide you with one. Is he here or not?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Our decision is to leave it at that and adjourn. We'll administer the oath to him tomorrow in the afternoon when we reconvene. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. BOURGON
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. President. We'll be ready to proceed tomorrow afternoon.

utterances.speaker: MR. BOURGON
utterances.text: to be reconvened on Wednesday, the 17th day of September, 2008, at 2.15 p.m. 22 23 24 25

procedural_notes.text: --- Whereupon the hearing adjourned at 6.53 p.m.,
